title: Keep the optimizer and the actual consumer execution separate
statement: For PSDprimitives and simplex theta,F=c*theta+b*(alpha I+sum theta_j B_j)^-1b is convex. Actual residual/action errors supply simultaneous gradient intervals; U=sum theta_j(ghat_j+delta_j)-min_j(ghat_j-delta_j) upper-bounds global regret. Coordinate scan/Frank-Wolfe step,curvature C=2L^2||b||^2/alpha^3,gradient radius<=epsilon_design/16 and2max(1,ceil(8C/epsilon_design))audited iterates give an explicit stopping algorithm,not arbitrary planning/eigen/solver advice. Source tolerance,failed solves,cache/error and finite arithmetic work remain charged. The executed consumer uses a fully charged noisy RICHARDSONsolver:16design iterations,1026source actions,gapbound.0091553/reference.0090647 for target.01. It tests the consumer interface,not an executed cache-reuse advantage for optimization.

requires: Unknown FIXED Hermitian primitives B_j, known norm bound L, actual chosen full-vector actions with ||error||<=delta||v|| at requested delta. Source reports need not be linear or independent.
Later adaptive A(theta)=alpha I+sum theta_j B_j has real sum|theta_j|<=1 and known A>=mu I; mu is supplied/earned from the input class, not inferred from a small compression.

Low-enrichment conclusion needs width of encountered task-action images at fixed epsilon/mu; unknown subspace/rank are analysis parameters, not learner advice. Correct acceptance does not require the width premise.

costs: At T tasks/R enrichments, explicit doubling/refresh schedule Q<=k(T+4R) primitive actions. Every failed solve and changing temporary load direction is included. Some already-contained tasks can cost zero new actions.
Column tolerance scales as sigma/sqrt(cache capacity); declared price delta^-p gives O_p(k sigma^-p[(R+1)^(1+p/2)+T(R+1)^(p/2)]). This is a proxy, not time/energy/sample count.
Storage O(knR), full-vector projections/output and reduced dense solves/QR paid. Squared Hermitian primitives use two original actions with propagated errors/preparation paid.
